findings.message: The `_pr_delivery_write_result` helper emits `draft` both at the top level of the result envelope and inside `data`; the ADR contract reserves the top-level for `result_contract`, `verdict`, `disposition`, `reason`, and `data`, so the top-level `draft` is schema pollution that could confuse strict consumers or schema validators — the old golden (written by pr-open) had `draft` only under `data`.

The `disposition` string read from the child plugin's result file (`merge-result.json` or `pr-result.json`) is passed through directly to the parent's v2 result without validating it against ADR-054's vocabulary; a child that writes a non-standard or empty disposition propagates unchecked into the engine's result table.

`stage_signal_begin` is installed at line 133, after the dry-run guard (lines 122–130); a SIGTERM that arrives during the dry-run path's `atomic_write` call will not trigger `_pr_delivery_on_signal`, leaving no result file — the dry-run path therefore has no signal protection despite `_PR_DELIVERY_ARTIFACTS_DIR` being set at line 84.

When pr-open returns `verdict=blocked`, the v2 result unconditionally writes `reason="review_signal_missing"` regardless of `_po_reason` captured from pr-open's result file; if pr-open ever blocks for a distinguishable reason, the actual reason is silently discarded (only the stage summary retains it via `${_po_reason:-blocked}`).

The `_mk_si` helper constructs ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS JSON via `printf '%s'` with file paths; any path that contains JSON-special characters (double quotes, backslashes, newlines) will silently produce invalid JSON and cause the block guard to silently skip input resolution — `jq -n --arg` should be used instead.
